library(haploStack)

## What this module does

The similarity module (`R/catalogue_similarity.R`) answers a breeding question:
**which markers reliably report whether a haplotype block was inherited from a
parent?** It has four pieces:

| Function | Role |
|---|---|
| `compute_segment_ibs()` | identity-by-state (IBS) of two haplotype segments |
| `compute_block_ibd()` | per-block parent→progeny IBD across a family |
| `score_marker_signal()` | per-marker TP/FP/TN/FN signal test (`IBD` or `IBS` mode) |
| `compute_signal_metrics()` | accuracy / precision / recall / specificity / F1 / MCC + MAF-weighted final scores |
| `select_signal_markers()` | the top `n` marker(s) of each block — the *signal markers* |
| `attach_signal_markers()` / `get_signal_markers()` | record that selection on the GenoMeta and read it back |

Two visualisations help pick candidates: `plot_marker_signal()` (a Manhattan of
a signal score) and `plot_signal_precision_recall()`.

### The comparison model

For each family, the comparison is **anchored on the parental haplotypes**: every
parental haplotype block (a family may have more than two parents — a
double-cross family with 4 parents has up to 8 parental haplotypes) is compared
against **every** progeny haplotype block. Block IBD is the ground truth
(`Similarity >= threshold`, inclusive); per-marker allele identity is the
prediction. The confusion matrix uses the standard orientation:

|             | IBD true | IBD false |
|-------------|----------|-----------|
| marker same | TP       | FP        |
| marker diff | FN       | TN        |

`mode = "IBD"` fills the cells with integer counts; `mode = "IBS"` fills them
with similarity-weighted fractional sums (`TP += same x Similarity`, etc.).

## A worked example

We build a small GenoMeta whose offspring genuinely inherit parental block
haplotypes, so the IBD signal is real.

```{r build}
set.seed(42)
n_mk    <- 20L
markers <- paste0("m", seq_len(n_mk))
bases   <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")

# Four founder haplotypes (parent P1: haps 1-2, parent P2: haps 3-4)
founder <- replicate(4L, sample(bases, n_mk, replace = TRUE))   # n_mk x 4

samples   <- c("P1", "P2", paste0("O", 1:6))
arr <- array(NA_character_, dim = c(length(samples), n_mk, 2L),
             dimnames = list(samples, markers, c("1", "2")))
arr["P1", , 1] <- founder[, 1]; arr["P1", , 2] <- founder[, 2]
arr["P2", , 1] <- founder[, 3]; arr["P2", , 2] <- founder[, 4]

# Two blocks; each offspring haplotype inherits a founder block-haplotype
blk <- rep(c("B1", "B2"), each = 10L)
for (o in paste0("O", 1:6)) for (h in 1:2) {
  hap <- character(n_mk)
  for (b in unique(blk)) {
    idx <- which(blk == b)
    hap[idx] <- founder[idx, sample(4L, 1L)]
  }
  arr[o, , h] <- hap
}

map <- data.frame(Chrom = "1", Marker = markers,
                  Pos = seq(1e4, by = 1e4, length.out = n_mk))
bmm <- data.frame(Chrom = "1", Marker = markers, Block = blk)

meta <- new_geno_meta(
  geno_arrays = arr, map_info = map, block_marker_map_info = bmm,
  metadata = list(ploidy = 2L, char_dict = c(A = 1L, C = 2L, G = 3L, T = 4L),
                  n_samples = length(samples), n_markers = n_mk,
                  source_format = "nucleotide", encoding = "nucleotide"))

# Attach a family: P1 x P2 -> O1..O6
fam <- data.frame(IID = samples,
                  Father = c(NA, NA, rep("P1", 6)),
                  Mother = c(NA, NA, rep("P2", 6)))
meta <- attach_family_history(meta, fam, parent_cols = c("Father", "Mother"))
```

### Segment IBS

```{r ibs}
seg_a <- arr["P1", 1:10, 1]
seg_b <- arr["O1", 1:10, 1]
compute_segment_ibs(seg_a, seg_b)
```

### Block IBD

`compute_block_ibd()` returns one row per pairwise (ParentHap x ProgenyHap)
comparison.

```{r ibd}
ibd <- compute_block_ibd(meta, threshold = 0.5)
head(ibd)
```

### Marker signal score and metrics

```{r signal}
sig <- score_marker_signal(meta, mode = "IBD")
names(sig)                 # detail / marker / metrics / signal
head(sig$metrics)
```

`mode = "IBS"` weights the confusion cells by block similarity instead of using
the hard IBD call:

```{r signal-ibs}
sig_ibs <- score_marker_signal(meta, mode = "IBS")
head(sig_ibs$metrics[, .(Marker, TP, FP, TN, FN, mcc, final_mcc)])
```

The final score `final_<metric> = metric x MAF x (1 - MAF)` down-weights
near-monomorphic markers (where a high metric is uninformative).

## Choosing the signal markers

Scoring ranks every marker; the *selection* step turns that into a decision —
the `n` marker(s) that represent each block. `score_marker_signal()` already did
it (`n_signal = 1` by default) and returned it as `sig$signal`;
`attach_signal_markers()` records it on the container, in
`block_info$Signal_Marker` / `Signal_Score` / `N_Signal`.

```{r select}
sig$signal                                   # Block, Marker, score_val, rank
meta <- attach_signal_markers(meta, sig$signal)
head(meta$block_info)
get_signal_markers(meta)                     # tidy read-back
```

The selection travels with the object: `filter_geno_meta()` prunes markers that
leave the panel, `save_geno_meta()` round-trips it, and re-running
`attach_block_info()` drops it (with a message) because new block definitions
invalidate a selection made against the old ones.

## Visualising the signal markers

The Manhattan highlights exactly the selected markers, and the block strip along
the top names the blocks they represent. Marker labels and the title are off by
default so the vertical block labels stay legible.

```{r manhattan, fig.alt="Manhattan of marker signal score"}
p <- plot_marker_signal(sig$metrics, geno_meta = meta, score = "final_mcc")
p
```

Every plot carries the marker × block table behind it, and
`save_marker_signal()` writes both under one name — `marker_signal.png` next to
`marker_signal.csv`:

```{r signal-table}
head(attr(p, "signal_table")[, .(Chrom, Pos, Marker, Block, is_signal,
                                 score_val, block_score, block_n_markers)])
```

```{r save-signal, eval=FALSE}
save_marker_signal(p, "marker_signal.png")
```

```{r prscatter, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, fig.alt="Precision-recall scatter coloured by MAF"}
plot_signal_precision_recall(sig$metrics)
```

Markers toward the top-right of the precision-recall plot, coloured for high
MAF, are the strongest candidate tags of block inheritance. The same flow scales
to real pedigrees: read genotypes with `read_plink_ped()` (or another
`read_*()`), attach a block map with `attach_block_info()` (or build LD blocks
locally with `hapS_ld_blocks()`), attach the pedigree with `attach_family_history()`, then
run `score_marker_signal()`.
